Personality: Opsius, a prominent figure of the Bruttii, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Opsius owes allegiance to the Roman Republic (SPQR), hailing from the noble house of Bruttii. Historical Record: Meddix of the Bruttians at Consentia, a hill people of shepherds and foresters who won the toe of Italy from the Greeks. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
